newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sending small security team to aid Haiti.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sending small security team to aid Haiti.

text.p: The United States is sending 30 diplomatic security agents to Haiti to help augment the security of President Rene Preval while he reorganizes his own security operation, administration officials said Friday.
The decision follows reports accusing members of Preval's security force of carrying out political executions, the officials said.

"We have substantially augmented our earlier force of approximately 10 security agents to a level we believe is sufficient to accomplish our training and security objectives around the clock," said State Department spokeswoman Julie Reside.

Reside said Washington viewed the murders as "a matter that requires intensive investigation," and said the United States had received assurances from Preval that his government would address the matter.
The U.S. security agents were not expected to stay in Haiti longer than a few months, she said.

Reside said State Department security agents and private U.S. contractors had been in Haiti for some time under an arrangement worked out with former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide before his return to power.

The Washington Post reported in Saturday editions that the operation would cost $3 million, and quoted a spokesman for Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms, a North Carolina Republican, criticising the plan.
"This is a textbook example of what we mean when we talk about pouring U.S. tax dollars down a rat hole," Helms' spokesman Marc Thiessen told the paper.
Administration officials said Preval requested stepped-up assistance from the United States while new agents were being trained to replace those being removed from the force.
